title: Embedder Onramp: Sprint Battle‑Stitch Deck (WIP)
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable sales deck + battlecard hybrid to win embedded inference pilots for developer platform customers (embedded SDK + hosted/dedicated migration path).

Audience: Integration architects, platform engineers, lead SEs running 30–60 min discovery + demo.

High level narrative (3 acts):
- Act 1: Fast validation — show a working embed path in 1 hour, predictable latency baseline, and cost ballpark.
- Act 2: Safety & compliance guardrails — private deployment triggers, data residency, KMS/HSM integration.
- Act 3: Scale plan and economics — batch profiles, caching, quantization tradeoffs, reserved capacity options.

Slide 1: Title + one‑liner
- Title: Embedder Onramp — 1hr pilot to prove app economics
- Speaker note: Set expectation — goal is a deployable PoC that demonstrates latency and unit cost within two weeks.

Slide 2: Why embed (customer pain)
- Bullet: In-app prompts need <150ms p50 for token generation to keep UX feeling native.
- Bullet: Cloud costs balloon if we can't cache prefixes or tune batching.
- Bullet: Security/regulatory teams block external APIs — need private deployment route.
- Speaker note: Call out concrete examples (chat widget, search reranking, code assistant).

Slide 3: Fast path options we demo
- Option A: Hosted API + local SDK prefix caching (fastest time to demo).
- Option B: Dedicated pool with pinned model (predictable throughput, next step).
- Option C: Private VPC appliance (compliance gating long term).
- Speaker note: Emphasize same API surface across A/B/C. Seller line: "Start hosted, graduate private with no code change."

Slide 4: Demo plan (30–60 minute engineer run)
- Step 0: Quick discovery (3–5 min): target flows, SLOs, sensitive data?
- Step 1: Small sample dataset & prompt template (5–10 min)
- Step 2: SDK integration + local prefix cache (15–25 min)
- Step 3: Measure p50/p95, token cost estimate, and failure modes (10–15 min)
- Risk calls: network constraints, model selection mismatch.

Slide 5: Seller quick scripts (30s–60s bites)
- Opening: "We can get a working embed in your app inside an afternoon and show exact latency + cost for your traffic profile."
- For security owners: "Private deployment with KMS/HSM and audit logs — we’ll scope that in the followup week."
- For platform engineers: "You keep the same API surface as your growth team — SDKs are drop-in and toggle routing to dedicated pools."

Slide 6: Rapid objections and counters (battlecard style)
- Objection: "We can use public LLM APIs — why Redwood?"
  - Counter: predictable latency SLOs + reserved capacity for bursts; explicit per-token economics and caching.
- Objection: "Data security concerns."
  - Counter: define a two-phase plan: POC on hosted with strict masking, then private VPC with KMS if approved.
- Objection: "Cost seems high."
  - Counter: show the unit-econ slide (next) + batching and KV cache demo reduces 30–60% of token spend for common flows.

Slide 7: Unit economics snapshot (seller talking points)
- Show back‑of‑envelope: tokens per session, average token length, cost per 1k tokens hosted vs quantized on dedicated.
- Callout: prefix caching reduces generation tokens by X% (note: X varies by app; collect sample).
- Speaker note: be honest — use ranges, not hard guarantees.

Slide 8: Tech playbook (for SE/eng lead)
- Integration checklist: SDK add, prefix cache opts, metrics hooks (latency, cost/token), test harness.
- Rollout knobs: routing policy (latency-first / cost-first), canary % by traffic, auto-fallback policy (model variant).
- Quick link: sample telemetry dashboards (trace + token cost per request).

Slide 9: Pilot acceptance criteria (what success looks like)
- Latency p50 within agreed SLO or >20% improvement over baseline.
- Cost per active user projection within budget threshold.
- No high‑risk data exfiltration in logs; compliance checklist signed.
- Integration readiness: SDK in staging and routing toggled.

Slide 10: Two‑week roadmap post‑POC
- Week 0: POC validation, baseline metrics, executive readout.
- Week 1: Optimization (batching, cache profiles, quantization experiment).
- Week 2: Decide path (Hosted ops -> Dedicated reservation or Private deploy scoping).

Appendix: SE cheat snippets
- Quick curl to sample hosted API (redwood example), SDK init, cache toggle flag.
- Pilot telemetry query examples and sample dashboard URLs.

Open questions / TODOs
- Get a real prompt corpus from target customer for accurate caching win estimate.
- Decide default model variants to propose (cost/latency tiers).
- Confirm legal review timeline for private VPC pilots.

Notes to self (choppy):
- Need small 1‑page handout for exec: "what we deliver in week 0/1/2".
- Add quick ROI calc script (spreadsheet) to linked artifacts.
- Run a dry run of demo with Marco next Wed.

Quick Pilot Checklist (bulleted for SE):
- [ ] Sample traffic & prompt set collected
- [ ] Staging API key + SDK installed
- [ ] Latency/Cost dashboards wired to demo account
- [ ] Canary routing and fallback policy set
- [ ] Compliance gating: masking + log retention config

Speaker tone guidance: pragmatic, data-first, avoid model marketing fluff. Emphasize operational certainty and migration path.

Last updated notes: Iteration 0.2 — tightened pilot acceptance criteria and added seller scripts. Will convert to a 6‑slide quick deck after internal dry run.
